nodes.name: Hydrothermal growth of Co(OH)2
nodes.procedure: Co(OH)2 nanoarrays were grown on the nickel foam substrate through a simple hydrothermal reaction.
nodes.source_text: Co(OH)2 nanoarrays (Figure S1, Supporting Information) were grown on the nickel foam substrate through a simple hydrothermal reaction.

nodes.name: Phosphidation to CoP
nodes.procedure: Then the materials underwent an annealing process with PH3, produced by the thermal decomposition of NaH2PO2, resulting in a topotactic transformation into CoP nanoarrays that maintained the same morphology as the Co(OH)2 precursor.

nodes.source_text: Then the materials underwent an annealing process with PH3, produced by the thermal decomposition of NaH2PO2, resulting in a topotactic transformation into CoP nanoarrays (Figure S2, Supporting Information) that maintained the same morphology as the Co(OH)2 precursor.

nodes.name: Pt electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, Pt was deposited onto the surface of the CoP nanoarray via cathodic electrodeposition (denoted as Pt/CoP).
nodes.source_text: Subsequently, Pt was deposited onto the surface of the CoP nanoarray via cathodic electrodeposition (denoted as Pt/CoP).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm the phase of Pt/CoP remained aligned with CoP (JCPDS #29-0497) following electrodeposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns in Figure 1c additionally confirmed that... the phase of the material remained aligned with CoP (JCPDS #29-0497) following electrodeposition.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image reveals Pt atoms uniformly dispersed on CoP surface without agglomerations, with clear fringes of ≈0.266 nm aligning with (202) plane of CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the atomic image of Pt/CoP was captured through high-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM, Figure 1d)... revealed clear fringes with a spacing of ≈0.266 nm, aligning with the lattice spacing of the (202) plane of CoP substrates.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS-elemental mapping illustrates highly overlapping distribution of Co, P, and Pt, confirming homogeneous dispersion of Pt species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-magnification energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images in Figure 1e additionally illustrated a highly overlapping distribution of Co, P, and Pt, confirming the homogeneous dispersion of Pt species.

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS mapping shows overlapping distributions of Cl⁻ and OH⁻ on Pt/CoP surface post-activation, with Cl⁻ relative intensity about one-fifth that of OH⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) mapping images in Figure 3a,b revealed that, following activation in the Cl⁻ containing electrolyte, the distributions of Cl⁻ and OH⁻ on the surface of Pt/CoP overlapped...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectrum confirms Pt-Cl coordination with vibrational peak at ≈350 cm⁻¹; Pt-OH signal near 1075 cm⁻¹ diminishes; Co-P signal at 650 cm⁻¹ unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum of Pt/CoP (Figure 3d, red line) further confirmed the formation of Pt-Cl coordination structure, as evidenced by a vibrational peak at ≈350 cm⁻¹... the signals attributed to Co-P (650 cm⁻¹) do not show significant changes...

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-activation high-resolution XPS of Pt/CoP shows Pt 4f peaks at ≈72 and 75 eV (Pt²⁺) shifted 0.2 eV lower; distinct Cl 2p signal; Co 2p peaks positive shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution spectra of Pt 4f are depicted in Figure 3e. In addition to the signal from the Ni substrate, the peaks observed ≈72 and 75 eV were respectively assigned to Pt²⁺ 4f₇/₂ and 4f₅/₂... this pair of Pt²⁺ peaks exhibited a shift toward a lower binding energy of 0.2 eV... Coupled with the distinct Cl 2p signal in Figure 3f...
